chunks: Al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:
“In the salat of the two Eids, when the people are five or seven, then they perform the prayer in congregation just as they do on the day of al-Jumuʿah.”
And he said: “He performs qunut in the second rakʿah.”
He said: I said, “Is it permissible without a turban?” He said: “Yes, and the turban is more beloved to me.”

key_terms.أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ: more beloved or preferred to me
key_terms.صَلَاةِ: the ritual prayer being discussed here in the context of Eid
key_terms.عِمَامَةٍ: a turban worn on the head
key_terms.يَقْنُتُ: he performs qunut, the supplicatory standing invocation in prayer
key_terms.ٱلرَّكْعَةِ ٱلثَّانِيَةِ: the second unit of the prayer
key_terms.ٱلْجُمُعَةِ: Friday congregational prayer used here as the comparison
key_terms.ٱلْعِيدَيْنِ: the two Eid festivals, Eid al-Fiṭr and Eid al-Aḍḥā

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings on congregational Eid prayer, qunut, and wearing a turban in the hadith of Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives fiqh guidance regarding the salat of the two Eids, indicating that a small group may establish it in congregation similarly to Jumuʿah. It also mentions qunut in the second rakʿah and clarifies that praying without a turban is permissible, though wearing a turban is preferable.
